findings: Owner request 2026-11-09: practice long questions for Chapter 2 in the same format as the Physics chapter practice, long questions in the Computer Science Board shape (8 marks each) (English and Roman Urdu), written from the chapter; not printed in the book. 14 questions numbered 1-14; by section: 2.1 1, 2.2 1, 2.3 1, 2.4 2, 2.5 2, 2.6 2, 2.7 1, 2.8 1, 2.9 1, 2.10 1, 2.11 1.

Covers the parts of computational thinking with its real-life examples, identifying a problem, step-by-step solutions and evaluation, logic in computer science and decision making, propositions with worked truth values, the connectives AND, OR, NOT, truth tables for two and three propositions (worked), equivalence and non-equivalence by truth table, satisfiability of three expressions (worked), predicates and variables, propositional vs predicate logic, quantifiers over small sets (worked), the library model (relationships, rules, conclusions), inference and deduction. Exercise long questions are not repeated (different angle or parts). Every truth table and result was computed in Python from the chapter's AND, OR, NOT rules.
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson), verified by tools.py.
The Roman Urdu file has the same checkpoints, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets.
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
